mechanic: A room with two doors, each watched by a different witness for a different stretch: neither watch alone closes any of the time, and the two together leave what neither covers.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose. Written for finding 124: the narrowing of when a deed could have been done, for a place with more than one door.

frame.says: A gold repeater laid on the table of the garden room at four was gone at eight; the room has two doors, one on the passage and one on the terrace.

questions.asks: Who took the watch from the garden room?

rules_out.Mr. Farrant: c.terrace and c.passage: the terrace door was shut while he walked past it, and after dusk he was in the passage
rules_out.anyone before dusk: c.passage and c.terrace together: neither door opened

clues.source: Ellen Wray, in the passage from four until eight
clues.says: The passage door did not open once; Philip sat by her until dusk and was not seen again until the gong; Mr. Farrant was with her from dusk until eight.

clues.source: Dunn, the gardener, on the terrace from four until dusk
clues.says: The terrace door was shut the whole time; Mr. Farrant walked the terrace from five and never touched it; at dusk Dunn went home.
